Article Title: Bankipur bypoll: Prashant Kishor adds a dash of yellow to Bihar palette of saffron & green
Article Text:
Jan Suraaj party workers celebrating Prashant Kishor's victory





PATNA: Bihar has been green. It has been saffron. Now Prashant Kishor brings yellow.Kishor, architect of poll victories for others, has finally written one for himself, winning his electoral debut in the Bankipur bypoll. It is a signal flare and perhaps a glimpse of a shifting political palette as Jan Suraaj broke through BJP’s saffron and RJD’s green duopoly.Born in Rohtas in 1977, Kishor studied in Buxar, completed his Class XII from Patna Science College, earned a BBA from Lucknow University and a master’s in healthcare management from ASCI, Hyderabad. He did a French language course in France before spending eight years in a UN-supported public health programme.National prominence came after helping design PM Modi’s successful 2014 LS campaign. His organisation, I-PAC, went on to work with multiple political parties. He advised former Bihar CM Nitish Kumar, former Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee and parties across Punjab, Andhra and Tamil Nadu, earning a reputation as one of the country’s most successful political consultants.After helping the Nitish-led Mahagathbandhan win in 2015, Kishor briefly joined JDU before returning to grassroots politics.A self-professed believer in Gandhi’s philosophy, he spent nearly two years on a padayatra across Bihar before launching Jan Suraaj Party on Oct 2, 2024. Its candidates drew a blank in the 2025 state polls, raising questions over whether his campaign skills could translate into votes.Barely eight months later, the answer arrived in Bankipur. Defeat would have dealt a crushing blow to both Kishor and Jan Suraaj. Instead, victory fuelled debate over whether Bihar has room for a third political force.“I did not contest to become an MLA or turn Bankipur into a metropolitan city like Bengaluru,” he said. “I wanted to send a message to BJP brass — generate employment, provide education and stop migration, or be prepared for similar results.”Married to Dr Jahnavi Das and father to a son, Kishor lives like a monk on campaign. He rarely watches TV news, hasn’t used a laptop in a decade, and relies only on his phone to stay connected with his grassroots network.
Article Summary: Prashant Kishor, architect of poll victories for others, has finally written one for himself, winning his electoral debut in the Bankipur bypoll. It is a signal flare and perhaps a glimpse of a shifting political palette as Jan Suraaj broke through BJP's saffron and RJD's green duopoly.

NEW DELHI: BJP Tuesday seized upon independent MP Pappu Yadav's depiction of a saffron clad sadhu who steals offerings and opposition MPs dragging him as part of a skit to hit back at its rivals for "insulting" Hinduism and asserted that they will suffer political consequences for their "unpardonable" act.The Purnia MP had staged the skit on Parliament's premises to target BJP for the embezzlement of offerings made by devotees at the Ram temple in Ayodhya, but his role-play of a sadhu has drawn disapproval even from within opposition and given the governing party an opening to reiterate its accusation that its rivals often insult Hindu sentiments.SP MP Ram Gopal Yadav said the skit should not have happened as sadhus had nothing to do with the theft of donations.Slamming opposition, BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra asked if opposition MPs would have dared to show priests of any other religion in a similar manner. "Not only India but the world would be jolted if religious leader of any other religion is seen to be dragged and beaten up as a thief. Your insult of Hinduism on Parliament's premises is unpardonable. Time will tell about its consequences as the battle is yet to begin," Patra said in a likely reference to UP assembly polls.

Article Title: After opening golf tournament, CM Omar says authorities must not allow repeat of migrant worker killings
Article Text:
Omar Abdullah, the chief minister of Jammu and Kashmir, strongly condemned the recent violence against migrant laborers, emphasizing that such acts are unacceptable and calling for heightened security measures. He also underscored the significance of golf tournaments as a means to boost tourism in the area, recalling a time when these events were a hallmark of Kashmir's serene landscape, well before militancy took root.

SRINAGAR: Jammu & Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah said on Tuesday that the recent attack on migrant labourers in south Kashmir’s Kulgam district “should not have happened” and that those responsible for maintaining security must ensure such incidents do not recur.“It is a matter of great regret… Innocent people were killed, and no religion permits such acts. No amount of condemnation or words is enough to denounce this attack,” Omar said.Under the Union Territory arrangement, law and order and security is looked after by lieutenant-governor Manoj Sinha.On July 31, terrorists had shot and killed two migrant labourers in Kulgam district. On July 23, a terrorist had shot J&K head constable Ashiq Hussain Qureshi dead in south Kashmir’s Anantnag, the first attack in Kashmir since the Pahalgam massacre that left 26 people dead on April 22 last year.The chief minister, speaking after inaugurating the fifth edition of the J&K Open 2026 DP World Professional Golf Tour of India (PGTI), said the golf tournament is an important part of his govt’s broader strategy to promote tourism. “Even without actively promoting golf tourism, we have started seeing what we want, people flying into Srinagar for a long weekend of golf,” he said.When asked about Article 370 and whether its abrogation has brought any change, like holding such tournaments, Omar initially declined to comment, saying the issue was unrelated to the event. He, however, said golf tournaments were organised regularly in Kashmir long before Article 370 was abrogated, and even before militancy began. “Golf tournaments were being organised in Kashmir even in the 1980s, much before militancy,” he said.
Article Summary: Omar Abdullah strongly condemned the recent violence against migrant laborers. He also underscored the significance of golf tournaments as a means to boost tourism in the area. He recalled a time when these events were a hallmark of Kashmir's serene landscape, before militancy took root.

Article Title: Lionel Messi: “I want to thank him and tell him that the people of Madrid hope to welcome him”: How the Inter Miami star’s €80,000 donation is helping rebuild Madrid’s wildfire-hit Sierra Oeste
Article Text:
Lionel Messi: “I want to thank him and tell him that the people of Madrid hope to welcome him”: How the Inter Miami star’s €80,000 donation is helping rebuild Madrid’s wildfire-hit Sierra Oeste

Lionel Messi’s €80,000 donation will support Sierra Oeste de Madrid’s recovery

Sierra Oeste de Madrid suffered widespread destruction after massive wildfires

Lionel Messi’s charity work goes far beyond football

Donation comes after Lionel Messi’s World Cup campaign and Inter Miami return

Lionel Messi has once again stepped forward to support people in need, this time by donating €80,000 to help rebuild Spain’s Sierra Oeste de Madrid after the region was hit by one of the worst wildfires in its history. The donation was confirmed by Isabel Díaz Ayuso, President of the Community of Madrid, who thanked the Argentina captain for his contribution. The money will go towards rebuilding communities damaged by the fires, which destroyed homes, forced thousands of people to leave their properties and left large parts of the region badly affected. The gesture comes just days after Messi returned to action for Inter Miami following Argentina’s run to the 2026 FIFA World Cup final.Isabel Díaz Ayuso announced Messi’s donation in a post on X, where she thanked the football legend for helping the affected communities.She wrote: “Leo Messi has donated €80,000 for the reconstruction of the Sierra Oeste de Madrid. I want to thank him and tell him that the people of Madrid hope to welcome him soon to give him the applause he deserves.”According to regional authorities, representatives from Messi’s team contacted the Community of Madrid to find the right way to make the contribution.The funds will be used as part of the reconstruction work already underway in the wildfire-hit area.The Sierra Oeste region, located west of Madrid, faced widespread damage after the fires swept through thousands of hectares of land. Several towns were affected, with homes destroyed or damaged, while tens of thousands of residents had to evacuate or remain under movement restrictions until conditions improved.The regional government has already announced emergency recovery measures, including housing support, repair assistance and rebuilding plans for affected families. Messi’s donation adds to those efforts as authorities continue restoring damaged communities and public infrastructure.Helping communities during difficult times is nothing new for Messi. Through the Leo Messi Foundation, which he created in 2007, he has supported projects focused on children’s health, education and access to sport.Over the years, he has also contributed to hospital projects, disaster relief and humanitarian campaigns in different parts of the world. His latest donation follows that long record of charitable work, with the Sierra Oeste contribution becoming another example of his support beyond football.Messi’s contribution comes shortly after he returned to play for Inter Miami following Argentina’s appearance in the 2026 FIFA World Cup final.The 39-year-old scored eight goals during the tournament as Argentina reached their third World Cup final in the last four editions. Although Argentina finished runners-up after losing 1-0 to Spain in extra time, Messi quickly rejoined Inter Miami to begin the next stage of the MLS season.Now, while getting back to club football, the Argentine captain has also made sure to support families trying to rebuild their lives after the devastating wildfires in Madrid.
Article Summary: Lionel Messi has donated €80,000 to help rebuild Madrid’s wildfire-hit Sierra Oeste de Madrid. The donation was confirmed by Isabel Díaz Ayuso, President of the Community of Madrid. Money will go towards rebuilding communities damaged by the fires, which destroyed homes, forced thousands of people to leave their properties and left large parts of the region badly affected.

Article Title: ‘Please listen to us’: Archie Goodburn’s emotional live TV plea sparks Andy Burnham response after tearful brain cancer appeal
Article Text:
‘Please listen to us’: Archie Goodburn’s emotional live TV plea sparks Andy Burnham response after tearful brain cancer appeal

Andy Burnham responds after Archie Goodburn’s emotional appeal

Archie Goodburn says current brain cancer support is still not enough

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Scottish swimmer Archie Goodburn’s emotional appeal for better brain cancer research has received a direct response from Prime Minister Andy Burnham. Days after Goodburn urged the government to do more for brain cancer patients during an emotional BBC Breakfast interview, Burnham invited the Commonwealth Games swimmer to a personal meeting. The 25-year-old, who was diagnosed with inoperable brain tumours more than two years ago, has become one of the strongest voices calling for better research, more clinical support and greater access to life-changing treatment. His message has now reached the highest level of government, with Burnham saying he wants to hear directly from him.Goodburn’s emotional interview with BBC Breakfast, later shared on TikTok, showed him asking the government to make brain cancer a bigger priority. Fighting back tears, he said:“Andy Burnham, if you believe and want to make a change and a difference to the future of our country and our young population, please listen to us.Please establish a national brain cancer lead and give us a chance to fight for our lives because the things that patients are going through out there are unbelievable and so unjust.There are clinical trials around the world, in the US, in Australia, in China, that could change lives. We are not seeing them in the UK and it is unfair and unjust.Please invest and make the difference. I’m on my knees begging for - not just my own life - but for those of my best friends and those that are affected and the families around the country.This has to change. It’s been going for too long and the suffering is unbearable.”Responding to the clip on TikTok, Burnham wrote:“Archie, thank you for this. I know how hard it must have been.What you’re doing for other people while you’re going through all this yourself shows the best of us.I’d really like to meet you and hear from you directly and I’ve asked my team to get in touch.”Earlier this year, the Rare Cancers Bill, led by MP Scott Arthur, became law to encourage more research and investment into rare cancers. But Goodburn believes it does not go far enough for brain cancer patients.“It’s a step in the right direction but it’s not going to make the changes that we need,” he said. “I’m extremely grateful for Dr Scott Arthur and the work he’s done there.“The rare cancers bill covers 14 different types of rare cancers. Brain cancer is one of these in terms of incidents of diagnosis, but it’s not the same in terms of the number of deaths it causes.“Yes it’s rare, but it’s extremely deadly. This frustrates me immensely.“The rare cancers bill establishes two new positions: a clinical lead and a research lead. These two roles are part-time across 14 different types of cancers and they accumulate to 36 days a year.“There’s two roles to cover 14 different types of cancer and change the landscape of treatment.“I do not see how 36 days a year is going to make that change for 14 different types of cancers, let alone the most deadly type of cancer.”Despite missing out on a medal at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, Goodburn said the support he received from the home crowd gave him hope. He also explained why he plans to keep speaking up for brain cancer patients.“It was an honour to compete in front of such a fantastic and supportive home crowd,” he said. “To see the support off the back of those interviews has been really, really touching and inspiring.”He added: “I partly feel like why we don’t hear so much about brain cancer and why the awareness is so poor is because patients unfortunately die so quickly.“I have this prognosis which is slightly longer and it’s given me this time to advocate - it’s two years since I was diagnosed.“I think when you’re really backed up against a wall like that there’s only really one way to go and that’s to go and fight.”
Article Summary: Archie Goodburn was diagnosed with inoperable brain tumours more than two years ago. He has become one of the strongest voices calling for better research, more clinical support and greater access to life-changing treatment. His message has now reached the highest level of government, with Burnham saying he wants to hear directly from him.

Article Title: Father quit Singapore job, pawned jewellery to fund chess dream: Olympiad-bound Savitha Shri's story
Article Text:
Savitha Shri will represent India at Women's Chess Olympiad this year (Special Arrangements)

It started with her brother, Mugesh

Savitha Shri at younger age (Special Arrangements)

Quitting a job in Singapore, and what came after

Savitha Shri (Photo by Michal Walusza)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

What comes next

Savitha Shri with brother Mugesh, mother Sarala, and father Baskar (Special Arrangements)

NEW DELHI: The last time the Indian women's team took part in the biennial Chess Olympiad, they won gold. The team consisted of Harika Dronavalli, Rameshbabu Vaishali, Divya Deshmukh, Vantika Agrawal, and Tania Sachdev. Two years have passed since that Budapest conquest, and India has now named its men's and women's squads for the 2026 edition in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. The name missing from the list took almost everyone by surprise. It was Harika Dronavalli.Confirming her decision to skip this year's Olympiad, Harika conveyed to TimesofIndia.com that she had already achieved what she wanted from the team event, a gold medal, and that her focus going forward would shift to individual tournaments.Meanwhile, her place has gone to someone 15 years younger than her. It is Savitha Shri, now 19, from Chennai."She's so happy to participate. Her main ambition is to participate in the event," her father, Baskar, told TimesofIndia.com during an exclusive interaction. "She already participated for the Indian team at the Asian Games before."That's indeed true. Savitha was part of the silver medal-winning women's team alongside Koneru Humpy, Harika, Vaishali, and Vantika at the 2022 Asian Games in Hangzhou.Reigniting those memories of the past, the 18-year-old, now with a more mature mind, will be replacing one of its most decorated names this September.Chess didn't arrive in the Baskar household through Savitha but through her older brother, Mugesh, five years her senior, whom their father originally set out to build a chess career around."We encouraged our son to play chess first," Baskar said. "For some years he was on that journey, state level, then national level."Savitha's introduction to the game happened as soon as he started sitting nearby, watching her brother play. "My Savitha was monitoring her brother, how he was playing, everything," her father added. "The interest came to her automatically. She wanted to play chess too."By the time Savitha turned six, both children were training under RB Ramesh, one of India's most respected chess minds, and his wife, Aarthie Ramaswamy, sometimes through free group coaching sessions the couple ran. But given that chess is an expensive sport, a family can only stretch so far, financially or otherwise, and a decision eventually had to be made."We couldn't manage two chess careers; I couldn't take the risk of splitting our support," Baskar said. "Savitha was also playing well, so I chose to help her continue her journey."Mugesh stepped back from competitive chess after the eighth standard. He has since finished university and started working. In the field of 64 squares, Savitha kept going.As Savitha's chess journey began to find its wings, it was then that Baskar, who had been working as an electrician in Singapore, chose to give it up entirely and return to India to support his daughter's chess career."Taking that decision was very difficult," he said. He'd hoped the transition back would be smoother than it turned out to be. "After I came back to India, I found it very difficult to manage the family and support her sporting career at the same time. I faced many, many issues."Some of those issues were straightforwardly financial. To fund a national tournament's entry fee at one point, the family had no choice but to pawn Baskar's gold jewellery.Even wider family support wasn't guaranteed early on. "In Savitha's childhood, our own family members, our brothers and sisters, weren't encouraging us to continue with chess," Baskar admitted, pointing to how much the sport was costing a middle-class household to sustain.It is part of why Baskar, who once represented Tamil Nadu in first-division cricket himself, steered both his children toward chess rather than the sport he knew personally."Cricket is teamwork; it's very difficult to shine without a lot of outside support," he said. "Chess is fully about a player's own talent."A bigger test came around 2022–23, when Savitha qualified for the World Rapid Chess Championship in Kazakhstan, a trip the family needed roughly three lakh rupees to make, money they didn't have.It was Savitha's school, Velammal, stepping in through its correspondent, that ultimately funded the trip. She repaid that faith by winning bronze, the youngest player in the field to medal.Sponsorship has followed its own uneven arc. A company backed Savitha's travel through 2023 and into 2024, before the support abruptly stopped. "I don't know why they stopped it suddenly," Baskar said. The two years that followed, through March 2026, were financially difficult, with fewer tournaments and performances that suffered as a result.Relief arrived only this April, when Savitha qualified for a Tamil Nadu government financial support scheme based on her results. "That's the only sponsorship we have right now," Baskar said. "That's what we're managing with."On where it all leads, Baskar doesn't hedge."I would like to see her become a professional chess player," he said. "We cannot stop it now."It is a family of six, the two siblings, their parents, and grandparents, under one roof, held together by a cricketer father's decision to bet everything on a daughter who first fell in love with the game by watching her brother play it.Whatever happens in Samarkand, we will be watching Savitha Shri Baskar. The world will be watching her too.
Article Summary: Savitha Shri, 19, will represent India at Women's Chess Olympiad this year. Savitha was part of the silver medal-winning women's team at the 2022 Asian Games. Her father, Baskar, gave up his job in Singapore to support his daughter's chess career.

Article Title: 'You drop me': Ex-cricketer says Rohit Sharma has thrown the ball into selectors' court
Article Text:
India's Rohit Sharma (ANI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former India cricketer Mohammed Kaif believes Rohit Sharma has made up his mind not to retire from ODI cricket on his own and will instead leave it to the selectors to decide when his journey with the national team should end.Rohit's future has been under intense scrutiny since India's ODI series against England. Reports ahead of the tour claimed that the senior selection committee had informed the veteran opener he was not part of India's plans for the 2027 ODI World Cup, with the selectors keen to invest in younger opening options, including Yashasvi Jaiswal The speculation gathered further pace after Rohit managed a slow-paced 26 off 47 balls in the second ODI at Cardiff. Questions over his future intensified, with reports suggesting the series decider at Lord's on July 19 could be his final ODI appearance for India.However, BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia dismissed those claims before the match, stating that no decision had been taken to make the Lord's fixture Rohit's farewell game. While the clarification ended immediate speculation, it did not confirm whether Rohit remained part of India's long-term plans leading up to the 2027 World Cup.The veteran opener responded in style, smashing 138 from just 110 deliveries during India's chase of 388 at Lord's. His innings, featuring 17 fours and five sixes, made him the first Indian batter to score an ODI century at the iconic venue, although India eventually fell 27 runs short and lost the series 2-1.Following the match, captain Shubman Gill said Rohit had not informed the team about any retirement plans, while Rohit himself insisted his only focus was on scoring runs for India.Sharing his views on the situation, Kaif said Rohit's recent actions suggest he has no intention of stepping away voluntarily.“Yes, one thing has become clear,” Kaif said during a discussion. “Rohit Sharma is effectively saying, ‘If I am not playing well, you take the call yourselves. Drop me.’“The fact that he has not stepped away or announced his retirement, the enthusiasm he is showing, the way he is approaching his batting and the hundred he scored at Lord’s — all of this shows that he is now focused entirely on playing. Whatever the selectors want to do after that is up to them. Perhaps earlier there was an attempt to convince him about certain things internally. The problem at the moment is that it is difficult to understand who stands where. There is a lot of confusion,” Kaif said on his YouTube channel.Kaif also questioned the lack of clarity from the team management regarding Rohit's long-term future. While coaches have repeatedly backed the opener to play with freedom, the former India batter believes the management should clearly state whether Rohit remains part of its World Cup plans.“At times, members of the coaching staff come out and say, ‘We have given Rohit Sharma complete freedom to play his natural game.’ But nobody has yet made a clear statement saying, ‘Rohit Sharma is part of our plans for the 2027 World Cup.’ That statement also needs to come. Rohit Sharma’s form will naturally go up and down. He may have a poor series, but the management must say that it is standing behind him.“Along with giving him freedom, they should also clearly say that they support him. Since no such statement has been made, there is considerable confusion and a lot of doubt. We are sitting outside, so we do not know exactly what is happening internally. But it appears to me that Rohit Sharma has now decided that he will not walk away on his own,” he added.Kaif pointed out that Rohit has already shown in the past that he is willing to make difficult decisions for the benefit of the team.After leading India to the 2024 T20 World Cup title, Rohit retired from T20 internationals. He later opted out of the fifth Test against Australia in Sydney in January 2025 amid a prolonged lean patch before announcing his retirement from Test cricket in May that year.Referring to those decisions, Kaif said Rohit has already twice put the team's interests ahead of his own.“Twice, he has taken the decision himself,” Kaif said. “After winning the 2024 T20 World Cup, he stepped away from the format and said that it was time to give an opportunity to the next generation. Then, during the Test series in Australia, when he was not scoring runs, he left himself out. After returning to India, he also retired from Test cricket. Those were decisions he took himself. But this time, Rohit Sharma appears to be saying, ‘You drop me. Even if it is humiliating for me, that is fine. You take the decision.’ That seems to be the situation now.”Kaif also praised BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia for publicly dismissing reports that the Lord's ODI would be Rohit's farewell match, saying the statement prevented unnecessary speculation from overshadowing the game.“The report that the Lord’s match could be his final ODI was also framed as a possibility. There was a question mark attached to it. But when such reports emerge, they can quickly become much bigger. The BCCI did a very good job by making a statement before the Lord’s match. That intervention became a turning point. There may still be confusion internally — perhaps even among the selectors — about whether to retain him or not. But no final decision has been announced.“Rohit Sharma should now be given complete freedom to play his game. The BCCI’s statement ensured that the entire focus at Lord’s returned to the cricket. Otherwise, every visual would have fuelled more speculation. People would have said, ‘Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma are sitting together and looking very serious, so this must be Rohit’s final match.’ Those rumours would have grown further. The BCCI stopped that narrative at the right time. The BCCI secretary came forward and made a statement, and he deserves credit for that.”Kaif concluded by urging the BCCI to evaluate every recommendation independently rather than accepting every opinion from the selection committee or team management.“The BCCI must also understand that the people it hires — whether they are part of the management, the selection committee or the coaching staff — are not necessarily right on every occasion. They may all be former India players who earned great respect and did a lot for the country, but that does not mean every piece of advice they give the BCCI will always be correct.”
Article Summary: Rohit Sharma's future has been under scrutiny since India's ODI series against England. Reports claimed the senior selection committee had informed the veteran opener he was not part of India's plans for the 2027 ODI World Cup. The speculation gathered further pace after Rohit managed a slow-paced 26 off 47 balls in the second ODI at Cardiff.

Article Title: 'You told Vaibhav Sooryavanshi to serve water': Ex-India star says he should have debuted in Ireland
Article Text:

Former India batter Mohammad Kaif believes young opener Vaibhav Sooryavanshi should have made his international debut during the Ireland series instead of being introduced in England. Kaif feels the 15-year-old would have settled into international cricket better if he had got an opportunity in Ireland first.Sooryavanshi earned his maiden India call-up after an outstanding IPL 2026 season. He was picked for the tours of Ireland and England but did not get a game in Ireland. After Sanju Samson struggled with the bat, the team management handed Sooryavanshi his debut in England. However, the teenager had a difficult start, scoring 14, 13 and 15 in the three T20Is he played before being left out of the fifth and final match.Kaif, who represented India in 13 Tests and 125 ODIs, said Sooryavanshi's confidence would have been much higher had he been given his debut in Ireland.“Vaibhav is an X-factor player. He made a reputation for himself. His bat did the talking in the IPL despite him being in the spotlight. He didn't just perform in one or two matches. He won the Orange Cap. He should have played in Ireland; the nervousness would have gone in that case. He would have reached England and performed well,” Kaif said on his YouTube channel.“He was having a rich vein of form behind him; he had won the Orange Cap.But you told him you serve water first. He's a special player; you could have played him directly in Ireland. He should have gotten special treatment. If he played in Ireland, he would not have had any nervousness in the UK.”Following his three low scores against a star-studded England side, Sooryavanshi was dropped for the fifth and final T20I, with Samson returning to the playing XI.Sooryavanshi responded impressively during the T20I series against Zimbabwe. He began the tour with a half-century in the opening match, scored 20 in the second game and then smashed 81 off 49 balls in the third T20I as India completed a 3-0 series sweep. The left-hander finished with 151 runs in three matches at an average of 50.33 and was named the Player of the Series.Kaif believes the youngster's international journey was made more difficult than it needed to be.“He didn't perform well in England; you dropped him. Sooryavanshi was playing against Archer. He hasn't played in India yet, but I am sure he will score a lot of runs when he plays here. Sooryavanshi's India journey was tough; it could have been made easier.”“It was made tough for him. He's a special talent; you shouldn't have dropped him. You should have played him in Ireland. Now see, against Zimbabwe, he won the Player of the Series award,” Kaif said.
Article Summary: Former India batter Mohammad Kaif believes Vaibhav Sooryavanshi should have made his international debut during the Ireland series. Kaif feels the 15-year-old would have settled into international cricket better if he had got an opportunity in Ireland first. The left-hander earned his maiden India call-up after an outstanding IPL 2026 season.

Article Title: NBA rumor: Warriors linked to land 6-foot-7 veteran alongside former Jimmy Butler teammate

Prince Ali bin Al Hussein lists three obstacles during Jordan’s historic World Cup debut

3. Unpaid FIFA Arab Cup prize money

Prince Ali bin Al Hussein accuses Gianni Infantino of ‘blackmail’

Jordan’s first-ever FIFA World Cup appearance was a historic moment for the country, but Jordan Football Association president Prince Ali bin Al Hussein says the experience was also filled with challenges off the pitch. In a statement shared on social media, the former FIFA vice president listed three major obstacles his federation faced during the tournament: visa problems for fans, tax costs linked to playing in the United States and unpaid FIFA Arab Cup prize money. He also accused FIFA president Gianni Infantino of “blackmail,” claiming he was told that supporting Infantino would help Jordan’s football federation. FIFA was approached for comment bybut had not publicly responded.Prince Ali said Jordan’s World Cup journey was made more difficult by three issues that affected both the federation and its supporters.Prince Ali said many Jordan fans were unable to travel to the United States because they were not granted visas despite already having match tickets. He also claimed that tickets were sold at “exorbitant prices,” making it even harder for supporters to attend the tournament.The second issue, according to Prince Ali, was the tax burden Jordan faced because the team was based in the United States during the World Cup. He said the federation was taxed by the U.S. government through FIFA and argued that the money should have gone to the players and staff instead. He added that teams which set up camp in Canada and Mexico did not face the same costs.Prince Ali also said Jordan is still waiting to receive the prize money for finishing runners-up to Morocco in the 2025 FIFA Arab Cup in Qatar.“The money our team should receive for having reached the final has not been delivered yet,” Prince Ali wrote, “while at the same time FIFA brags about how many billions they have in reserve.”After listing the three issues, Prince Ali said FIFA had refused to help Jordan on these matters for months. He then claimed that during the World Cup, he was told backing FIFA president Gianni Infantino would improve the federation’s situation.“It was verbally communicated to me during the World Cup that if I endorsed Infantino it would go a long way to helping our FA out.”Prince Ali said Jordan chose not to change its position despite that message.“We pride ourselves in Jordan in upholding ethical values. We did not endorse him before and certainly will not now.”“But the whole situation amounts to blackmail and we refuse to give in to that.”The allegations come as Infantino faces growing pressure over his leadership following criticism of his proposed World Cup investment plan. FIFA has set November 18 as the deadline for candidates to enter the next presidential election, which is scheduled to take place on March 18 in Rabat, Morocco. FIFA has not publicly responded to Prince Ali’s claims.

Article Title: Streamer D4vd's old fake blood promotional video resurfaces after latest murder case courtroom revelations
Article Text:
A resurfaced promotional video showing D4vd wearing a fake blood-stained shirt has gone viral following new developments in his ongoing murder case. The clip gained renewed attention after prosecutors referenced items allegedly found during the investigation. D4vd's defense argued the fake blood was tied to his merchandise and creative projects. A judge has ruled there is enough evidence for trial, while the singer has pleaded not guilty to all charges.

D4vd promotional video resurfaces after court hearing

D4vd continues to deny allegations as trial moves forward

A promotional video released long before D4vd's legal troubles has resurfaced online, attracting renewed scrutiny after details from a recent court hearing emerged. The clip, originally created to promote the singer's merchandise and upcoming album, has become a major topic of discussion because of evidence referenced by prosecutors in the ongoing criminal case against the artist. While online speculation has intensified, D4vd has pleaded not guilty to all charges.The resurfaced video shows D4vd, whose legal name is David Anthony Burke, wearing a shirt designed to look stained with fake blood while shopping for laundry detergent. The shirt was part of merchandise tied to his music promotion, and the clip was originally intended as a creative marketing campaign.Interest in the video increased after prosecutors outlined evidence during a preliminary hearing in the murder case involving Celeste Rivas.According to prosecutors, investigators discovered an inflatable pool inside D4vd's garage that allegedly carried the odor of laundry detergent. They also said a crumpled dryer sheet was found inside the pool. Those details quickly prompted comparisons online between the court testimony and the older promotional video.The renewed attention has fueled widespread discussion across social media, with many users pointing to the timing of the resurfaced clip.However, the video itself predates the legal proceedings and was produced as part of the artist's promotional work.D4vd's legal team addressed the issue in court, arguing that the presence of fake blood found inside his home was connected to his merchandise and other creative projects. The resurfaced video has since been cited by supporters as evidence that fake blood and similar props were already part of his artistic work before the criminal investigation.The renewed online attention comes shortly after a judge ruled there is sufficient evidence for D4vd to stand trial.Prosecutors allege that in April of last year, Burke arranged for Celeste Rivas to travel by Uber to his Hollywood Hills residence. They further allege she was fatally stabbed before her body was dismembered. According to court filings, her remains were later discovered inside two bags in a Tesla months after she disappeared.Burke now faces charges including murder, continuous sexual abuse of a child under the age of 14 and unlawful mutilation of human remains.He has pleaded not guilty to every charge.The preliminary hearing also brought additional investigative details into public view, prompting another wave of online commentary surrounding the case. While prosecutors maintain the physical evidence supports their allegations, the defense has continued challenging how some of that evidence has been interpreted, particularly regarding the fake blood used in D4vd's creative projects.As the case moves toward trial, the resurfaced promotional video has become another focal point of public discussion. Even so, the video's circulation on social media does not alter the legal process.The allegations against Burke remain unproven in court, and the upcoming trial will determine whether prosecutors can establish their case beyond a reasonable doubt. Until then, the resurfaced footage continues to generate online debate while legal proceedings move forward.

Article Title: ‘I am still living’: Georgina Rodríguez answers ‘body-shaming’ critics as Cristiano Ronaldo’s private words come to light
Article Text:
‘I am still living’: Georgina Rodríguez answers ‘body-shaming’ critics as Cristiano Ronaldo’s private words come to light

Cristiano Ronaldo’s fiancée Georgina Rodríguez explains why she refuses to let body-shaming define her

Georgina Rodríguez says she exercises for happiness, not to meet society’s expectations

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Recent photos of Cristiano Ronaldo ’s fiancée Georgina Rodríguez enjoying time on a boat led to a wave of comments about her appearance on social media. While many fans defended her, others criticised her body, prompting the model to share a personal message on Instagram . Instead of responding to individual comments, Rodríguez spoke about motherhood, confidence and why she refuses to let strangers decide how she should feel about herself. She also revealed what Ronaldo told her during a private conversation, saying his words reminded her that her value is far greater than physical appearance. Her post focused on accepting change, raising confident daughters and rejecting unrealistic beauty standards.Rodríguez said she understands that her body will continue to change and believes that should never be seen as something negative. As the mother of six children, including three daughters she shares with Ronaldo, she said she wants her children to grow up knowing that self-worth should never depend on appearance or the opinions of strangers.She wrote:“My body will change, just like every woman’s body changes. And I hope it continues to do so for many years, because that will mean I am still living. I am the mother of six wonderful children, three of whom are girls who will one day become great women. And if there is one thing I want to teach them - along with Cris, whom I feel deeply proud of for the values he passes on as a father and as a man - it is that a person’s worth can never depend on their physical appearance or the opinions of strangers.That small dose of positive psychology that I try to give them every day also helps me continue finding my way in a world filled with so much illusion.”Rodríguez also shared that the criticism upset her because people often judge her only through her public image. She said Ronaldo reminded her that the qualities that truly matter cannot be measured by appearance.She wrote:“And he replied: ‘You don’t make a living from your image. You make a living from who you are. A perfect woman. Beautiful, with an amazing body, a mother, a good person, successful, and someone who lives life with love. What more could you want? It’s normal that people envy you. And we talked about many other things too.’”Rodríguez also spoke about how the same discussion returns every summer, with people once again focusing on her body. She questioned who decides what the “right” body should look like and rejected the idea that happiness has a certain size. She said going to the gym is something she does because it makes her feel good, not because she wants to meet anyone else’s expectations.She continued:“The curious thing is that this happens every summer. Every year, my body becomes news again. And then I ask myself… where is the standard? Who decides what the “right” body is? Do we really still believe that happiness has a size? I work out because it makes me happy… I love my curves.I love the freedom of living in the body I choose.The body that supports me, that has allowed me to embrace, create life, fall down, and get back up again. A body that deserves respect, love, and gratitude in all its forms.”Rodríguez ended her message by saying she is thankful for everything her body has carried her through, from motherhood to life’s challenges. She said real success comes from inner peace, good health and meaningful relationships, not from trying to match unrealistic beauty standards.
Article Summary: Georgina Rodríguez says she exercises for happiness, not to meet society’s expectations. She says she wants her children to grow up knowing that self-worth should never depend on appearance or the opinions of strangers. Her post focused on accepting change, raising confident daughters and rejecting unrealistic beauty standards.

He told reporters in Oxnard that Fant will miss the entire season. The team plans to wait until the MCL settles down before moving forward with surgery.Schottenheimer sounded disappointed for the player more than anything else. While speaking to reporters after practice, he said, “Really disappointed for him, for everything that he’s put into this.” He also told Fant that his story is far from over and added that doctors believe he has a strong chance to make a full recovery.That stance carried extra meaning because Fant has already dealt with a major knee injury. According to reports, he sustained a similar injury in high school in Tennessee, which caused him to miss most of his junior and senior seasons. That earlier setback forced him to rebuild his career long before he reached the NFL, so this latest injury becomes another difficult chapter in a journey that has already included major adversity.Princeton Fant entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent from Tennessee and has spent the last three seasons with the Dallas Cowboys. Most of his work came on special teams and as a depth tight end. He has played in 11 career games and has not recorded a reception, but coaches valued his blocking ability and physical style.That is why this injury hurts more than the stat line suggests. Princeton Fant entered camp with a real opportunity to strengthen his place on the roster behind Jake Ferguson and Luke Schoonmaker. Coaches viewed him as one of the better blockers in the tight end room, and that role mattered in both the running game and special teams.Now the Dallas Cowboys must reshuffle the position group. Brevyn Spann-Ford, Michael Trigg, and DJ Rogers should receive more reps during the rest of camp and the preseason. Trigg and Rogers, both undrafted rookies, suddenly have a much bigger chance to prove they can contribute as blockers and special teams players.The frightening scene on the practice field created immediate concern, and the official diagnosis confirmed the worst fear. Princeton Fant’s season is over, and the Dallas Cowboys lose an experienced depth player just as training camp competition begins to intensify. For Fant, the focus now shifts from making the roster to tackling a long rehab process and working his way back onto an NFL field.
Article Summary: Dallas Cowboys confirm Princeton Fant suffered a season-ending ACL and partial MCL injury. Fant entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent from Tennessee and has spent the last three seasons with the Dallas Cowboys. Brevyn Spann-Ford, Michael Trigg, and DJ Rogers should receive more reps.

Article Title: Luka Doncic vs Anamaria Goltes: What's going on with Lakers star's child support case with ex-fiancée?

Luka Doncic as ex-fiancée reportedly drops child support battle

Luka Doncic's child support case took a significant turn this week after his ex-fiancée, Anamaria Goltes, reportedly withdrew her California petition seeking child support for their two daughters. The filing hints at a potential shift away from a courtroom battle and toward a private resolution between the former couple.The development comes just days before a scheduled court date and follows months of legal back-and-forth over jurisdiction, custody, and financial support. While the dismissal does not end the broader dispute, it suggests both sides are now attempting to settle matters outside the California court system.Anamaria Goltes filed documents on Monday asking a Los Angeles judge to dismiss her child support petition without prejudice, according to TMZ. The move allows the issue to be revisited in the future if necessary, but for now reflects an effort to reach an agreement away from the courtroom."I am withdrawing my Petition for Child Support with the specific intention of resolving this matter amicably and by a mutual agreement which is in the best interests of our children," Goltes stated in court documents obtained by TMZ.Her decision follows Luka Doncic's legal challenge to the California filing. Through attorney Laura Wasser, the Los Angeles Lakers star reportedly argued that the petition lacked legal grounds because the children have been living in Slovenia rather than California. Court filings also claimed Doncic encouraged Goltes to relocate to California with their daughters, but she chose to remain in Slovenia, where the children have lived since May.The legal process, however, has not been entirely straightforward. According to TMZ, Goltes' request to dismiss was initially rejected because the paperwork did not include Doncic's signature, leaving procedural matters to be resolved before the filing can be finalized.ESPN also reported that Goltes withdrew the petition ahead of an Aug. 14 court date after being required to submit a responsive pleading. Sources familiar with the situation told the outlet that custody proceedings remain active under the jurisdiction of Slovenian courts.Doncic and Goltes were together for approximately a decade before ending their engagement, with reports indicating that long-distance challenges played a role in the separation. Today, the former couple share two daughters, Gabriela and Olivia.Although the child support petition has been withdrawn, no details have been disclosed regarding any private agreement involving financial support, custody arrangements, or parenting responsibilities as of now.The family matter has also influenced Doncic's offseason plans. According to ESPN, the 27-year-old chose to remain in Slovenia this summer instead of representing his national team in the FIBA World Cup European qualifiers."I love my daughters more than anything, and they will always come first in my life," Doncic posted after the Lakers' playoff exit. "As I continue working toward joint custody of my daughters, I have been forced to make a difficult decision between traveling and playing for the Slovenian national team and being with my daughters this summer."With custody proceedings continuing in Slovenia and the California child support petition now moving toward dismissal, the legal focus appears to be shifting overseas. Meanwhile, Doncic is expected to host the Lakers for a four-day minicamp in Ljubljana later this month, balancing preparations for the upcoming NBA season with an offseason centered on family.
Article Summary: Lakers star Luka Doncic's ex-fiancée Anamaria Goltes reportedly withdrew her child support petition. The move hints at a potential shift away from a courtroom battle and toward a private resolution. The former couple share two daughters, Gabriela and Olivia.

Article Title: “Allar trying to spin like Rodgers”: Steelers QB Drew Allar embarrasses himself with wild training camp mistake while Will Howard steals the spotlight

Drew Allar’s shocking training camp miss sends Steelers fans into a frenzy as Will Howard steals the spotlight(Getty)

Viral throw puts Drew Allar’s development under the spotlight as Will Howard gains attention

Drew Allar became one of the biggest talking points from Steelers training camp after a short video showed him missing a large practice net during a quarterback drill. In the video, Drew Allar released the ball while looking away from the target, and the pass sailed well over the net. The post reads, “Can't say I've ever seen a quarterback just outright miss the net."Many fans gave mixed reactions: One fan said, “Allar is trying to spin like Rodgers.”The second fan added, “He tried doing a Aaron Rodgers-type throw with the footwork lol.”The third fan said, “One of the worst throws possible by Allar, still struggling with his footwork.”Another fan wrote, “Howard is him. Allar is trying to spin like Rodgers 👎”One more fan added, “Howard looks pretty smooth.”The same clip also drew attention to Will Howard’s performance. Howard hit his target cleanly during the drill and looked more controlled through the motion.Many fans praised his footwork, balance and release, and several comments said he appeared more comfortable and more accurate than Allar during the sequence. Because both quarterbacks are competing for developmental snaps behind Aaron Rodgers, the comparison quickly became part of the discussion around Pittsburgh’s young passers.The Pittsburgh Steelers selected the former Penn State quarterback with the 76th overall pick in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft. The team drafted him for his size, arm strength and movement ability, not because he arrived as a polished NFL quarterback.Analyst Jim Wexell recently said Drew Allar still looks like a developmental passer, citing decision-making, touch, and footwork as the areas that need the most improvement. “Big, strong kid who can move, stand in the pocket, throw a great deep ball,” Wexell said during a recent training camp evaluation discussed by Steeler Nation. “Decision-making, finesse game, that’s really key. So, that’s going to have to come along a long way. ”That evaluation aligns with the main concern about Drew Allar’s game. His deep ball creates excitement, but NFL coaches will judge him on the routine throws, quicker decisions and cleaner mechanics that keep an offense on schedule. Reports from Steelers camp say head coach Mike McCarthy has emphasized footwork and mechanics through his quarterback development program, often called “QB School.”The coaching staff has focused on connecting each drop with the route concept and improving timing and balance.Aaron Rodgers remains the clear starter. The real discussion sits behind him. One throw will not decide whether Drew Allar or Will Howard becomes the Steelers’ future quarterback, but the clip brought fresh attention to the same developmental questions that McCarthy and the Steelers coaching staff are trying to answer during training camp.

Article Title: French trans basketball star Julie Tétart hopes to join WNBA following Sophie Cunningham’s controversial statement
Article Text:
Julie Tétart. Image via: Getty Images

Julie Tétart is eyeing a move to the WNBA

Julie Tétart dominated France's Ligue Féminine 2

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Julie Tétart's WNBA hopes gain spotlight amid Sophie Cunningham's comments

Julie Tétart, the French transgender basketball player who led her league in scoring and rebounding this past season, says she would accept a WNBA contract if one came her way. The comment surfaced as the league continues wrestling with a separate controversy involving Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham, whose remarks opposing transgender participation in women's sports sparked protests, a suspension, and White House attention over the past several weeks.Tétart, who plays center for Monaco Basket Association in France's Ligue Féminine 2, told reporters she wasn't holding her breath but wouldn't turn down the opportunity either.Tétart's numbers from the 2025-26 LF2 season made the question worth asking. She averaged roughly 21 points and 20 rebounds per game, leading the league in both categories while playing at 6-foot-3. Despite that production, she was passed over for MVP, though she still collected Player of the Year, Defensive Player of the Year, and Domestic Player of the Year honors.Asked directly whether she'd consider trying out for a WNBA roster, Tétart didn't dismiss it. "I won't say no," she said. She followed that by noting the realistic obstacles facing a 34-year-old crossing over from a second-tier European league, pointing out that plenty of players in the WNBA are simply better equipped for that level. “But you have to be realistic: I'm old, and there are far better players than me!" Tétart told OutKick.Her dominance wasn't limited to a strong statistical average. During one March game, Tétart posted 21 points and 30 rebounds, setting a new league rebounding record and breaking her own previous mark. Such production is part of why French trans advocacy groups pushed back hard when she was left off the league's MVP ballot, a decision that also excluded fellow trans player Aurore Pautou despite her own strong season.Tétart addressed the possibility of a WNBA future carefully, calling it a longtime aspiration shared by any young female basketball player, but adding that circumstances outside the sport make it unlikely. She pointed to broader political conditions in the United States, without going into detail, as the sticking point rather than anything about the league itself.The timing put Tétart's comments squarely inside an ongoing WNBA debate. Cunningham, a seventh-year guard for the Fever, drew national attention after telling ESPN she supports keeping transgender athletes out of girls' and women's sports, framing her stance as protective rather than hostile. She stood by the comments the next day, telling reporters, "I said what I said. I think it's kind of common sense."Not everyone in the league agreed. Fever head coach Stephanie White pushed back on framing exclusion as any kind of solution, saying, "I don't ever believe that exclusion is an answer," while acknowledging she didn't consider herself well-versed in the underlying science. Minnesota Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve went further, later telling reporters, "I come from a space of inclusion," and wearing a shirt reading "Trans Kids Belong" during a game against Indiana.Whether Tétart ever gets an actual roster offer remains an open question. For now, her answer stands on record, and the league's ongoing debate over transgender inclusion shows no sign of settling before training camps open.
Article Summary: Julie Tétart led France's Ligue Féminine 2 in scoring and rebounding this season. The 34-year-old center says she would accept a WNBA contract if one came her way. The comment surfaced as the league continues wrestling with a separate controversy involving Sophie Cunningham.

To avoid being seen in restaurants, he would pay private chefs £200 to £300 per hour to come to his apartment and cook, but they were never of Indian origin, and it was never the same chef twice, the podcast revealed."I don't think he was clever enough to come up with the (Punjab National Bank) scam himself," the source added. The podcast speculates that Nirav has submitted a second asylum case, which is why he has not gone back. Nirav's solicitor Anand Doobay, who Mallya also used, told TOI: "We are not commenting."

Article Title: Meet Nathan Thomas: 18-year-old Florida teen becomes the world's youngest male professor after breaking a 306-year-old record
Article Text:
How Nathan Thomas became the world's youngest male professor

Image: CBS Miami

An extraordinary academic journey

A passion for engineering and teaching

Looking beyond engineering





An inspiration for young learners

At an age when many students are just beginning university, Nathan Thomas had already stepped into the classroom as a college professor. The Florida native earned a place in the Guinness World Records after becoming the world's youngest male professor at just 18 years and 346 days old, breaking a record that had stood for 306 years. Thomas joined Miami Dade College as an engineering instructor, where he teaches students who are often close to his own age. His remarkable academic journey, which began with enrolling in college at the age of 10, has now made him one of the youngest educators ever to teach at the higher education level. His journey stands out not only for the record itself but for what it represents, a reminder that intellectual growth does not always follow a fixed timeline, and that curiosity, nurtured early, can open doors.Nathan Thomas officially became the world's youngest male professor when he accepted an engineering teaching position at Miami Dade College at the age of 18 years and 346 days. Guinness World Records confirmed that he surpassed the record previously held by Scottish mathematician Colin Maclaurin, who became a professor at the age of 19 in 1717. The achievement ended a record that had remained unbeaten for more than three centuries.Thomas began teaching COP 2270: C for Engineers at Miami Dade College in August 2023. The course introduces engineering students to the fundamentals of C programming and computational problem-solving. Many of his students are around the same age as him, but Thomas believes age matters far less than a willingness to learn. He has said that everyone enters the classroom with the same goal of gaining knowledge and improving their skills. His appointment also demonstrates that expertise and dedication, rather than age alone, can earn respect in higher education.Thomas displayed exceptional academic ability from an early age. At just 10 years old, he dual-enrolled at Miami Dade College while continuing his school education. By the age of 14, he had transferred to Florida International University, where he completed both bachelor's and master's degrees in electrical engineering with honours. His accelerated academic path eventually led him back to Miami Dade College, this time as a faculty member rather than a student.Coming from a family of engineers, Thomas developed an interest in mathematics and science at a young age. He has credited his mother with helping him understand mathematical concepts in ways that made learning enjoyable. He says the most rewarding part of teaching is watching students grasp ideas that once seemed difficult, describing those moments as just as satisfying as solving engineering problems himself.While continuing to teach, Thomas is also pursuing a Juris Doctor degree at the University of Miami School of Law, with an expected graduation in 2028. He hopes to combine his engineering background with legal expertise by specialising in intellectual property law, particularly in areas involving science, technology, engineering and mathematics. According to Thomas, the structured problem-solving skills he developed through engineering have proved valuable in his legal studies. As emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence continue to reshape industries, expertise spanning both engineering and intellectual property law is expected to play an increasingly important role in protecting innovation. By bridging engineering and law, he hopes to contribute to the protection of innovation in rapidly evolving fields driven by science and technology.Nathan Thomas's achievement demonstrates how determination, curiosity and a passion for learning can open extraordinary opportunities at a young age. From entering college as a child to becoming the world's youngest male professor and breaking a 306-year-old Guinness World Record, his journey has inspired students and educators alike. As he continues balancing teaching with law school, Thomas hopes to contribute to both education and innovation while encouraging others to pursue ambitious goals regardless of age.
Article Summary: Nathan Thomas became the world's youngest male professor at the age of 18 years and 346 days. The record had been held by Scottish mathematician Colin Maclaurin, who became a professor at 19 in 1717. Thomas is also pursuing a Juris Doctor degree at the University of Miami School of Law.

Article Title: “Three-against-one situation”: El Rubius opens up on being “targeted” in MrBeast’s viral $1M challenge
Article Text:
El Rubius reacted honestly after his elimination from MrBeast’s $1 million challenge, calling it “unfair” and claiming he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings. His response felt real and balanced, especially after MrBeast’s team later sent him a cake, softening the moment.

El Rubius reflects on a tough and “unfair” exit







El Rubius did not just walk away from MrBeast’s $1 million streamer challenge. He opened up. Soon after his elimination, the Spanish creator shared a raw reaction with fans, giving them a closer look at what the experience felt like from inside the game. It was not polished or carefully framed. It felt real, and that is exactly why it caught attention so quickly.The clip and his response have since fueled conversations across the streaming space. Some viewers believe intense competitions like this naturally lead to uneven situations. Others feel Rubius may have had a point about being singled out. Either way, his words have added a human layer to a challenge that many only saw as entertainment.Speaking through an Instagram Story, Rubius did not hide his frustration, but he also made sure to thank his supporters. He said, "Guys, I just got knocked out of the game. It was a bit of an unfair elimination, but hey, at least I managed to walk away with $50,000 for you all, which I’ve already distributed. It went to the mods, the subs, and the non-subs alike."He further added, "I’m happy, of course, though admittedly, it was incredibly tough.I wasn't really a fan of the challenge itself, either. But then again... it was basically a three-against-one situation the entire time. I mean, they were targeting me specifically the whole way through. I kept trying to go after RaKai, but, well, he actually just got eliminated in the end. So, at least justice was served for Abraham. Abraham, if you’re watching this, we were all rooting for you, and standing right there with you."His message carried mixed emotions. There was disappointment, yes, but also pride in how he handled things. Giving away his $50,000 winnings to his community stood out as a gesture that meant more than the result itself.He continued with another honest note, saying, "And in the end, karma finally caught up with that little punk. Sorry, I’m being a bit toxic right now, but let's just hope the MrBeast team doesn't see this! Guys, thank you all so much. Seriously, thank you for all the support and for just being there."He added, "Every time I asked for something in the chat or whatever it was, you guys were right there. You’re incredible. I’m a little disappointed in myself, personally, mostly for not performing better, but hey, I gave it my all, and we still walked away with $50,000, so we’ve got to look on the bright side. All right, guys, big hugs to all my brothers out there!"Interestingly, the story did not end with frustration. Later that day, Rubius revealed that MrBeast’s team had sent him a cake after his exit. It was a small gesture, but it shifted the mood. It showed that even in a high-pressure challenge, there is still room for respect.In the end, Rubius’ reaction felt honest and grounded. That is what stayed with people.
Article Summary: El Rubius was eliminated from MrBeast's $1 million streamer challenge. He called it "unfair" and said he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings.

Article Title: IPL craze costs techie Rs 1.46 lakh in fake RCB vs CSK ticket scam

RCB register their second win

But for a 25-year-old techie the craze for IPL tickets for RCB vs CSK turned too costly and he was duped for a massive Rs. 1.46 lakh.The techie, a resident of B Narayanapura, fell into a trap by a post posted by a fraudster who posed himself as a ticket seller on Instagram.As per a report in Deccan Herald, the techie alleged in a complaint to Mahadevapura Police that an individual claiming to be Sumit Biswal promised he could arrange IPL tickets along with food coupons.As per the techie, Biswal was introduced him as a senior supervisor for ticket counter at M Chinnaswamy Stadium"He asked me to come near the stadium gate number 10, saying someone would deliver the tickets within minutes, and even sent an email confirmation to gain my trust," the complainant told Deccan Herald."Initially, I agreed to buy two tickets for Rs 3,700 each,but he kept asking for more money under various pretexts such as refundable security deposits, additional ID cards and food coupons.Trusting him, I made multiple payments - even using my mother’s bank account after exhausting my own limits—and ended up transferring around Rs 1.46 lakh," he added.Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s incisive spell of 3-41, coming after a marauding batting show from Tim David, Rajat Patidar and Devdutt Padikkal, propelled Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) to a commanding 43-run victory over Chennai Super Kings (CSK) in their IPL 2026 encounter at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium on Sunday.The contest saw RCB’s batting unit dismantle CSK’s attack with relentless hitting, as David’s 70 not out off just 25 balls and Patidar’s unbeaten 48 off only 19 balls provided for the late fireworks after Padikkal’s fluent 50 off 29 balls had set the tone for the daunting total.Their combined effort lifted RCB to a daunting 250/3, thus setting a new record for highest total in IPL 2026. Article Title: Clavicular Viral Controversy: "Trans women are.....": Clavicular’s viral moment with trans women sparks fresh conversation on internet culture

The court also deferred the bail pleas of Vikas and Dinesh Biwal till then. Proceedings on taking cognisance of CBI’s chargesheet were also adjourned to the same date as the final report remains under scrutiny. CBI has charge-sheeted all 13 accused, currently in judicial custody.The three accused, Mangilal Biwal, Dinesh and Vikas, moved an application through their counsel, AP Singh, seeking permission to undergo both tests. “The applicants seek to assist the investigating agency by voluntarily offering themselves for recognised scientific examination, so that every lawful investigative avenue capable of aiding the search for truth may be explored,” the plea said, adding that the tests could be conducted at any govt-approved forensics laboratory.Tuesday also marked the first hearing before special judge Gupta, who was reassigned the court handling the cases under Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, including the NEET-UG paper leak case.
Article Summary: The three accused, Mangilal Biwal, Dinesh and Vikas, moved an application through their counsel, AP Singh, seeking permission to undergo both tests. Tuesday also marked the first hearing before special judge Gupta, who was reassigned the court handling the cases under Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act.

Article Title: Former Pakistan cricketers face possible PCB ban: Here's why
Article Text:
The PCB said it has taken "serious notice" of the participation of former Pakistan cricketers in the tournament.

NEW DELHI: Several former Pakistan cricketers could face disciplinary action from the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) after taking part in the Asian Legends League in Zambia without the required approval, according to ESPNcricinfo. More than a dozen retired Pakistan players signed up for the tournament. The controversy began after the Zambia Cricket Union (ZCU), the country's official governing body, said the event was not sanctioned, approved or endorsed by it.The PCB said it has taken "serious notice" of the participation of former Pakistan cricketers in the tournament.Players found to have violated the rules could be banned for two years from receiving a PCB No Objection Certificate (NOC) to participate in approved overseas leagues or cricket events.They could also be declared ineligible for any cricketing, coaching, consultancy, mentoring or other roles with the PCB and the Pakistan Super League (PSL) for two years."In light of the above, the following disciplinary measures will be taken on individuals found to have participated in the said unsanctioned event without obtaining the requisite approvals from the PCB," the PCB statement said. "A ban of two years from the issuance of any PCB No Objection Certificate (NOC) for participation in approved overseas cricket leagues or events.[And] Ineligibility for any cricketing, coaching, consultancy, mentoring and/or other assignments with the PCB and the PSL for a period of two years. "According to ESPNcricinfo, Mohammad Hafeez , Sohail Tanvir and Umar Akmal travelled to Lusaka after signing up for the league. However, they chose not to play after learning that the required ICC approvals had not been received.Several other former Pakistan cricketers are believed to have participated in the tournament.The PCB said all current and former Pakistan cricketers must obtain the required approvals before taking part in overseas cricket events."The PCB remains fully committed to upholding the ICC regulations and safeguarding the integrity and governance of the game," the PCB statement said."The board reiterates that all current and former cricketers seeking to participate in overseas cricket events requiring PCB clearance must obtain the necessary approvals and NOCs prior to participation," it said.
Article Summary: Several former Pakistan cricketers could face disciplinary action from the Pakistan Cricket Board. More than a dozen retired Pakistan players signed up for the tournament. The controversy began after the Zambia Cricket Union (ZCU) said the event was not sanctioned, approved or endorsed by it.
